# General Social Survey: agent index

A repeated cross-sectional survey of US adults, 1972 to 2024, about attitudes, behaviors and attributes.

Publisher: NORC at the University of Chicago. Dataset id: `gss`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://gss.norc.org/terms-and-conditions.html. LLM processing: `allowed`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the year; `form` is the ballot.

## Releases

| Release | Table | Variables | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `7224r3a` | - | 50 | GSS 1972-2024 Cross-Sectional Cumulative Data, Release 3a |

## Corrections applied

These records had an error in the source documentation. The shards show the corrected value; the JSONL `view.corrected` block gives the original, the problem and the confidence.

- `racfew` /questions/0/text (inferred): The question text stops mid-sentence.
- `rachaf` /questions/0/text (verified): A stray space after the hyphen in 'African- Americans'.
- `racopen` /questions/0/text (verified): The text of the two laws is missing, so the codes 'first law' and 'second law' can't be interpreted.
- `racschol` /questions/0/text (verified): The question text belongs to a different item; the value labels ('same schools', 'separate schools') don't match it.

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the full records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

Line form: `name | waves; forms | scale signature | label | question text`. Wave runs like `1972-1978` follow the waves present in the release, so a run skips years with no survey. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

Read `SKILL.md` before answering a question from these files.
